I haven't looked closely at how plotting works under the hood, but I think we will need to:

1) Define a graphics device interface and create an implementation based on java.awt.Graphics2 (see RJavaDevice, maybe we can reuse?)

2) Implement the graphics primitives, which I think most call down to the graphics device layer. (See the Graphics section in BaseFrame.java)

See http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-ints.html#Graphics-devices for a primer. 

Fortunately it looks like the lion's share of R's rich graphic functionality is written in the R language itself so we 

P.S. If possible i would like to keep Renjin's graphic device interfaces totally decoupled from java.awt.* because these classes are not available on the AppEngine environment.  For AppEngine, we could then implement a graphics driver which emits SVG directly to the browser.

Best,

Alex

also..

as i read, there are many platform dependent devices in R. For
instance png() function includes if statements for device type and the
current values are X11, cairo and quartz. X11 stands for X server,
quartz is for mac os. svn(), pdf() and ps() functions use the device
cairo. png(), svg(), ps(), pdf() functions handle the graphical works
on the fly, calling the dev.off() method finalized the entire job.

It seems, as Alex says, lots of work are done in R side with graphics
functions. R creates a visual windows by callign plot.new() with no
internal parameters and other functions (plot, hist, barplot. plot.ts)
do their jobs at the higher light layer.

Most of the job is to define and implement the device interface and
the basic devices, respectively.

I think i need Alex's job planning at this stage and i return to
implement other primitives.

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Graphicals
parts:
Hi Mehmet,

I think abstract base classes are useful if you expect the API to evolve over time (because it's easier to change abstract class without breaking implementations) or if there are lot of methods that can be implemented as functions of other API methods (like the InputStream API), but in this case the API seems quite simple so an interface might be the best choice.

As for the parameter types, see what is easier and more natural. I believe there's a "graphics engine" layer between the R code and the device layer. If this intermediary layer is relaying Vector SEXPs from the R code to the device layer then Vectors would probably be easier; if the intermediary layer is manipulating the arrays a lot then the other way may be more natural.

Awesome that you're looking into graphics!

I would start with a simple test like "barchart(1:5)"  and keep coding primitives until you get a nice picture. Don't worry too much about the structure of the code of the first draft-- with good test coverage it's easy and safe to refactor afterwards. Just add all the R globals like the par HashMap (graphics parameter) and the current device to the Context class.

Best,

Alex
